subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Cervical spine trauma and cord injury: C1-C2, ASIA, MAP and decompression
refs: AANS/CNS Cervical Spine Trauma and SCI Guidance

steps.say: Axial loading is bursting the C1 ring into a Jefferson fracture. Spread past seven millimetres is marking transverse ligament rupture by the Rule of Spence. Rupture is demanding C1-C2 fusion, not a collar.
steps.tx: **Jefferson fracture** of C1 follows axial loading with lateral mass spread, and combined spread above 6.9 mm by the Rule of Spence marks transverse ligament rupture needing C1-C2 fusion. An intact ligament allows collar care. Spread is measured on open-mouth views.

steps.say: The dens is breaking at tip, base or body in the Anderson-DAlonzo scheme. Base fractures past fifty or with backward slip are favouring posterior fusion. Collars are suiting stable tip injuries alone.
steps.tx: **Odontoid fracture**s are Anderson-DAlonzo type I tip, type II base and type III body, numbered 1, 2 and 3, with type 2 in patients above 50 years or with posterior displacement favouring posterior C1-C2 fusion over a collar. Blood supply at the base explains nonunion. Stable type 1 injuries heal in a collar.

steps.say: Hyperextension with axial loading is hanging the C2 body in bilateral pars fractures. Grade one is wearing a collar while grade two is reduced then held. Severe angulation is fixed at C2-C3 and traction is avoided in 2a.
steps.tx: **Hangman fracture** with traumatic C2 spondylolisthesis from hyperextension with axial loading is Levine-Edwards types 1 to 3 (I to III): type 1 collar-managed, type 2 reduced then held in halo or collar, and types 2a and 3 with severe angulation fixed at C2-C3. A disrupted disc makes 2a unstable despite appearances, and traction is avoided in 2a. Angulation plus translation forces surgery.

left.title: Types 1 and 2 (collar or halo)
points: Type 2: reduce then halo or collar

steps.say: The atlas is sliding forward when the transverse ligament is failing in Down or rheumatoid necks. Three millimetres in adults or five in children is proving instability. Posterior screws are then joining C1 to C2.
steps.tx: Atlantoaxial instability with an **atlantodental interval** above 3 mm in adults or 5 mm in children, common in Down syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis, needs posterior C1 lateral mass to C2 pedicle fixation. Flexion-extension views unmask reducible slip. Irreducible settling needs decompression too.

steps.say: Injury is graded A through E with sacral sparing deciding complete from incomplete. The neurological level is set at the lowest fully intact segment. Dermatomes are mapping that level at the bedside.
steps.tx: **ASIA grades** cord injury A complete through E normal, with the neurological level set by the lowest intact segment and sacral sparing distinguishing complete from incomplete injuries. Perianal sensation and voluntary anal contraction decide completeness. The chart is repeated as spinal shock resolves.

steps.say: Elderly hyperextension is producing weak arms with spared legs and sacral feeling. Anterior injury is taking pain with preserved position sense. Hemisection is splitting motor and pain to opposite sides.
steps.tx: **Central cord syndrome** after elderly hyperextension gives weak arms with spared legs and sacral sensation, anterior cord gives paraplegia with lost pain but spared proprioception, and Brown-Sequard hemisection gives ipsilateral motor with contralateral pain loss. Each pattern localises the lesion. Brown-Sequard carries the best prognosis and anterior cord the worst, while central cord recovers legs before hands.

rows: Weak arms, spared legs, sacral sparing

steps.say: Mean arterial pressure is held between eighty-five and ninety for a full week. High-dose steroids are no longer routine after reanalysis of the old trials. Complications of steroids are outweighing any signal of benefit.
steps.tx: **MAP 85 to 90** mmHg is held for 7 days after acute cord injury per AANS/CNS guidance, while high-dose methylprednisolone is no longer routine after NASCIS reanalysis. Cord perfusion is the modifiable target. Vasopressors maintain the range when fluids alone fail.

steps.say: Decompression within a day is improving outcomes with ongoing cord compression. Neurogenic shock is showing low pressure with slow pulse and warm skin. Fluids with vasopressors are correcting it, unlike blood loss.
steps.tx: STASCIS supports **early decompression** within 24 hours for cervical cord injury with ongoing compression, and neurogenic shock with hypotension plus bradycardia and warm skin is treated with fluids and vasopressors unlike hypovolemic shock. Bradycardia with warmth distinguishes it from bleeding.
